name: Pentecost and the Ministry of the Holy Spirit
path: New Testament Studies: Life and Doctrine in Christ
Acts and the Founding of the Church

objectives.text: Retell the story of the Holy Spirit coming at Pentecost with the sound of a rushing wind and tongues of fire
Name the Holy Spirit as the Helper whom Jesus promised to send to his disciples
Recall that Jesus told his disciples to wait in Jerusalem until the Holy Spirit came
Recall that Peter preached about Jesus at Pentecost and that about three thousand people were baptized
Locate on a map several of the nations listed in Acts 2 to show that people from many lands heard the gospel in their own languages
Summarize the events of Acts 2 in order from the coming of the Spirit to the baptism of the new believers
Explain how the gift of languages at Pentecost contrasts with the confusion of languages at Babel
Explain the setting of Pentecost as a Jewish harvest feast held fifty days after Passover
Compare Peter's denial of Jesus with his boldness at Pentecost and identify how Luke attributes the change to the Holy Spirit
Explain that the Holy Spirit is the third person of the Trinity, true God equal with the Father and the Son
Trace how the pattern of Acts 1:8 from Jerusalem to Samaria to the ends of the earth unfolds through the Spirit's work in Acts
Explain why Jesus said it was better for his disciples that he go away and how his ascension relates to the sending of the Spirit
Explain why the Reformed tradition describes Pentecost as a once-for-all event in redemptive history that marks the beginning of the new covenant church
Analyze how Peter uses Joel 2, Psalm 16, and Psalm 110 to argue that Jesus is both Lord and Christ
Interpret how Pentecost fulfills Joel's prophecy of the Spirit poured out on all flesh regardless of age, sex, or social status
Explain from Scripture that the Spirit gives gifts to believers for the common good of the church
Explain the response Peter called for in Acts 2:37-41 and how the Reformed tradition reads the promise to believers and their children in support of covenant baptism
Explain the Spirit's work of convicting the world concerning sin, righteousness, and judgment
Describe how the Spirit produces fruit in believers as part of the work the Reformed tradition calls sanctification
Explain how the Reformed tradition teaches that the Spirit applies Christ's redemption by uniting believers to him through faith
Explain the Spirit's work of illumination in enabling readers to understand Scripture
Construct an explanation of the Holy Spirit's role in missions from passages where the Spirit directs and empowers witness in Acts
Evaluate the distinction between the Spirit's permanent indwelling of every believer and the repeated filling of the Spirit described in Acts and Ephesians
Defend the personhood and deity of the Holy Spirit from Scripture against views that treat the Spirit as an impersonal force
Evaluate continuationist and cessationist interpretations of tongues and prophecy using Acts, 1 Corinthians, and the Westminster Confession
Synthesize the connection between Christ's Great Commission and the Spirit's empowering at Pentecost in a written argument

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies: the Pentecost narrative, the Helper, Peter's preaching, the nations, the Acts 2 summary, Babel reversal, fear versus courage, Peter's sermon, Joel 2, Spirit and witness, conviction, missions, indwelling versus filling, personhood, and the Great Commission link. Recast 'identify the birth of the Church' as an explanation of Pentecost's place in redemptive history. Dropped bare recall fragments by folding them into fuller objectives. Added the waiting in Jerusalem, the feast setting, the Trinity, the ascension and sending of the Spirit, spiritual gifts, the Acts 2:39 covenant promise, sanctification, union with Christ, illumination, and the continuation and cessation debate. Each item now has verse-level Scripture and confession anchors where they truly state the doctrine. Left community life and persecution, Paul's journeys, and Gentile inclusion to the sibling sub-topics.
